summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource and Logicoma, coded by Edhellon with music by H0ffman and Ferris's packer. It came second in the Oldskool Intro compo at Revision 2022.
why: A runner-up in a strong Revision oldskool intro compo, squeezing a run of colourful effects and a soundtrack into 4K on the often overlooked TED machine.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a 1930s gangster theme, winner of the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2025. Graphics by Talent, DeeKay and others, music by LMan, Psycho8580 and Magnar.
why: Sceners call it one of Censor's freshest and most stylish demos, singling out Talent's dithered graphics, the projector-noise film styling, new spins on Kefrens bars and Magnar's end tune. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2026.

quote.text: Everything in this demo is so damn slick, smooth, quick, flowy.  Looks effortless, even if I know there's shitloads of work behind it.

summary: Mahoney's demo for the Vectrex, the vector-display console, which won the demo compo at Isterparty 2014.
why: A compo winner on an unusual platform: the Vectrex draws everything as glowing vector lines rather than pixels, so it's a rare chance to see demo effects on a vector screen.

summary: Traction and Brainstorm's C64 one-file demo, coded by Preacher with graphics by Phase1 and music by Buzzer, placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Mostly black-and-white screens of text and images, opening with a Marshall McLuhan quote.
why: A first C64 demo from newcomers that sceners welcomed warmly, praising its atmosphere, Buzzer's tune and how fresh it looks despite a very limited colour palette. The source is available.
highlights: text hidden in ones and zeroes

quote.text: Also extremely cool how you stick to such a limited colour palette and still make all screens look fresh and appealing.

summary: Baze's 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro competition at Forever 2017.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2017, squeezing its full-screen visuals into just 1K of code.

summary: Co-Operation's demo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4, which won the demo competition at Árok 2006.
why: A compo winner on the Plus 4, a machine with a small but dedicated demo scene. It took first place in the Árok 2006 demo competition.

summary: Trilobit's Atari 2600 invitation intro for Outline 2009, coded with graphics and music by Ilmarque and text by visy. It won the Oldskool Intro compo at Numerica 2009.
why: A compo winner on one of the most restrictive platforms around, and an invitation from the VCS scene for the Outline party.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Speccy.pl and Lamers, tagged as a parody, that won the Combined Demo compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2013. Code by Tygrys, music by Ziutek on the AY, graphics by At0m.
why: It took first place in the combined demo competition at RetroKomp / Load Error 2013, and its parody tag points to a tongue-in-cheek take on the demo form.

summary: deMarche's demo for the ZX Sprinter, an enhanced Spectrum-compatible machine, which won the Combined Demo compo at Multimatograf 2025. Directed by Zeebr, with code by TmK, music by Nik-O and graphics by TmK, Rainman and Nodeus.
why: A first-place compo winner at Multimatograf 2025 and on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist, showing what the Sprinter hardware can do in a modern demo.

summary: Razor 1911's single-file C64 demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Code and design by rez, graphics by Kenët and Made, music by Ziphoid. The title is 1911 written in hex.
why: Sceners call it stylish and colourful, and nearly all of them single out Ziphoid's tune. Kenët and Made drew all the graphics specifically for this demo.

quote.text: Stylish and colorful demo. Awesome music by Ziphoid <3

summary: M&M's Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at S:T Lars Meeting 2007, built around a missing-person story, with code by MagerValp and music by zabutom.
why: Sceners remember it for its dark, creepy mood and its tie to a real missing-person case, and many single out zabutom's Boards of Canada cover, "Turquoise Hexagon Sun".

quote.text: Got reminded of this one today. Had to comment again. This demo stays in your mind. So moody.

summary: Genesis Project's Atari VCS demo, coded by Shadow with graphics and music by Mermaid, placed third in the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A compo-placing demo on the Atari 2600, a machine with very little to work with, from a group better known on other platforms.

summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by Trefi with music by nq, which placed second in the 8-bit demo compo at Multimatograf 2015.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, with the whole visual side down to a single person, Trefi.

summary: Performers' three-disk-side C64 music demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2016. It runs as a themed show built around a concert, with music from LMan, Linus, Mixer and others, and graphics by DeeKay, Bitbreaker, Redcrab and Veto.
why: Sceners single out the greetings part, which several call their favourite demo part ever, along with the cute kid-voice credits and LMan's Thrust remix. Many treat it as a music demo to replay for nostalgia.

quote.text: It feels like the C64 all-stars with all those familiar C64 game icons in one place.

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo that streams full-motion video with sound from a DivIDE interface. It won the Realtime Wild Demo compo at Outline 2010, and this recording is live footage from the party screen.
why: A compo winner that shows the Spectrum playing streamed video from a DivIDE, something the stock machine was never built for. The subtitles promise full details, including the player code and converter utility.

summary: Elysium's folk-themed C64 demo, made for the folk theme at Xenium 2024 and winner of the C64 demo compo there, with graphics by Joe, Mikael, Jetboy and Valsary and music by Shogoon and Randall.
why: Sceners single out the soundtrack, especially Shogoon's leads that sound improvised on a real instrument, along with the graphics and its cheerful countryside mood. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production and Best Soundtrack at The Meteoriks 2025.

quote.text: Huge breeze of fresh vibes with one of the most gorgeous soundtracks I've ever heard <3

summary: Fairlight and Offence's C64 demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014, with code by Pantaloon, music by Danko and graphics by Pal and Louie64.
why: Sceners single out the smooth organic tunnel, the Mr Fisk sprite and the vertical scroller, and several compare its attribute scrollers and Danko's music to a Censor Design demo.

quote.text: Great release, love the credits and the organic moving tunnel stuff.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, coded by Tygrys with graphics from Darklight, CatMan, Slayer and At0m. It took second place in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2017.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2017 with a large graphics team behind it, and a good look at what Polish Spectrum sceners were doing in 2017. CatMan provides the music as well as graphics.

summary: Extend and Dekadence's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2009, built around a run of twister variants with graphics by Duce and fragment and music by Barracuda.
why: Sceners single out the twisters, especially a grey-shaded one whose lighting looks almost photorealistic, and Duce's design. The IDM-leaning soundtrack divided opinion, but some found it kept getting better on rewatching.

quote.text: I find myself watching this again six months later, surely the mark of a great demo.

summary: Dekadence's C64 4K intro, coded by BriteLite and SounDemoN with music by SounDemoN, which won the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2005.
why: A Breakpoint compo winner, reviewed in Nordic Scene Review 1. The one CSDb comment singles out the strange sounds SounDemoN gets out of the music.

quote.text: A demon of sound truly he is. Something seriously strange about the sounds in the music there is.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014, with code by Bob, Lavazza and CRT, graphics from a large team including Leon, and music by Magnar.
why: Sceners rate it well above its 5th place, singling out the serpent ribbon part, Magnar's soundtrack, Leon's hires art and heavy VSP trickery made for the original breadbox C64.

quote.text: The serpent ribbons are really cool, and so are many of the other parts.

summary: Radiant's one-file C64 demo, placed 4th in the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2026: a song about Pouet's forum drama, with the lyrics typed out over a cartoon pig on a field of trumpets.
why: Sceners love it as a song with lyrics, a joke about Pouet threads set to a SID tune and presented as a small demo. Jammer also pointed out a clever use of colours to mask sprites.

quote.text: What a lovely way to present a message, or tune for that matter! The world needs more sid's with lyrics!

summary: SerzhSoft's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum Tiny Intro (256b) compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions in the 256-byte category, one of the tightest size limits on the Spectrum.

summary: NOOP's first C64 demo, a humorous 'pimp my bento' story that won the Real Wild compo at Assembly 2015. A lunchbox gets assembled ingredient by ingredient, ending with portraits of the crew.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a fresh, funny debut, praising its cartoonish graphics, fun texts and the unexpected tentacle. It was nominated for New Talent at The Meteoriks 2016.

quote.text: A good mixture of 1985 graphics, a weird but fresh and very enjoyable story, some nice effects and some nice humor.

summary: Atari 2600 demo by Digital Sounds System, coded by Tjoppen with music by Knoeki, which came 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2012.
why: A sample-playback showcase on the VCS: the on-screen text claims 1 min 10 sec of 5-bit PCM at 3 kHz squeezed into 32 KiB, with a podium place at Stream 2012.

summary: Insane is a 1997 ZX Spectrum 48K demo by 3SC, with code by Baze and Astex and graphics and music by Baze, using AY sound. It's tagged as running on the TK90X, the Brazilian Spectrum clone.
why: An early demo from 3SC, with Baze handling code, graphics and music himself. It's well liked on Pouët, with no thumbs down.

summary: Skrju's monochrome ZX Spectrum demo, winner of the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2007, with graphics by tanya_2308, music by nq and code by sq.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2007, and it's a good example of a demo built on a mood and a strict monochrome look rather than on effects.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that came second in the demo compo at Floppy 2003, with code by Hollowman, graphics by Hollowman and Tempest, and music by Goto80.
why: Sceners call it stylish and modern, single out Goto80's music and its neat screens, and JackAsser credits it with drawing him into C64 coding.

quote.text: I just love this demo. :) It sucked me in to C64 coding.

summary: Nuance's Vectrex demo, coded by Nitro, which won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012. Wireframe vector graphics glow on the console's built-in vector screen.
why: A compo winner on a rarely used platform, and a chance to see demo effects drawn on the Vectrex's vector display instead of a raster screen.

summary: Dual Crew's C64 demo on a white background, coded by Zaz with music by Jan Harries, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners single out the colour-filled hires vectors, including an Elite Thargoid and a final object in six colours with black outlines, along with the clean design and Jan Harries' tune.

quote.text: These color-filled hires vectors are visually the tastiest I've ever seen. I love the font animation too.

summary: An invitation demo for the NOVA online party by Bitshifters and Torment for the BBC Master, which placed second in the Demo compo at Outline Online 2020.
why: A runner-up in the Outline Online 2020 demo compo, coded by Henley and Kieran with music by Rhino. It carries an epilepsy warning, so expect flashing visuals.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation demo by Lamers for Silly Venture 2018, with code by MKM and Szeryf, music by XTD and graphics by Moonwalker. It placed 8th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018.
why: A party invitation that went on to compete at Revision, made by a team of Polish Atari regulars. Worth a look for how it promotes the Silly Venture party through big chunky text and animation.

summary: Gods of the Universe's two-disk-side demo for the Commodore Plus/4, which won the demo compo at Árok 2018. Code by Lavina and Ati, graphics by Harry, Shadow and DLST, music by Celticdesign.
why: A first-place demo from Árok, the Hungarian party, and a substantial two-disk-side production for the Plus/4, with three graphicians credited.
highlights: waving logo over a dotted backdrop

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2019, opening with Dane's huge multiscreen ring picture before a run of scrollers, zoomers and an Amiga-ball vector.
why: Sceners single out Dane's spiralling intro picture, the rotating scroller and the colourful zoom scroller, calling it a worthy winner packed with top-notch routines, even if some found it short.

quote.text: The intro is awe-inspiring, setting the stage for an onslaught of awesome complicated routines.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper, that came third in the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012.
why: A podium finish in a mixed low-end compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012, where it was placed against prods from other 8-bit machines.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010, with graphics by Louie64, code by Abaddon and Pantaloon, and a zabutom remix of a Dubmood tune.
why: Sceners praise Louie64's graphics, especially the suited skeleton man, along with the stylish design, the music and the isometric rising and falling pillars. Several welcomed it as a strong debut from Fairlight's PC demo section.

quote.text: the pace and the sync to the music is great, not to speak of that skeleton. Also love the overall design! outstanding demo!!

summary: A joint Atari XL/XE demo by New Generation and Zelax that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 WE. It needs 1MB of RAM and features shaded 3D objects.
why: It was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, which the Demozoo notes call a world first for an Atari 8-bit production.

summary: Extend's two-disk-side C64 demo, crashed on the compo machine at Zoo 2024 and then released in final form at Transmission64 2024, where it won the demo compo. It is built around an animation player with heavy VHS-style video distortion and all-border pictures.
why: Nominated for Best Visuals at The Meteoriks 2025. Sceners call it video art rather than a conventional demo and praise how the visuals react to the sound, though some find it repetitive over its length.

quote.text: This is just stunning both visually and aurally (and how the visuals react to sound). Beyond C64 limits. My favourite C64 demo by far from this day on.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, released at Assembly 2014 where it placed third in the Real Wild Demo competition.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's Real Wild compo for the unexpanded-looking VIC-20 is a fair recommendation on its own. The fact sheet holds little more, so expect a short, curious watch.

summary: Five Finger Punch's Atari VCS demo, which won the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2023, with code by Vilcans, Morbid and Imodium, graphics by Corel and music by Triace.
why: A compo winner at Gerp 2023 that was put on the Meteoriks watchlist for 2024, which makes it one of the year's notable releases on the Atari 2600.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Satori, with code and music by Zden and graphics by BexBorder. It placed second in the Oldschool Intro compo at Riverwash 2018.
why: A compo-placed 4K intro on the Atari 2600, with its soundtrack made in TIA Tracker, the VCS's own music tool.

summary: Oof Heads' Atari 8-bit demo for the 130XE, coded by MKM with graphics by Odyniec1 and music by 505. It came second in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k25 WE.
why: A runner-up at the main Atari 8-bit party of 2025, and it was put on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.

summary: Oxyron's one-file C64 demo marking the group's twentieth anniversary, placed 2nd in the demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2011: a big Yazoo logo over a zooming scroller carrying greetings texts from the members.
why: Sceners praise Axis's zoom scroller, which casts a shadow, something one commenter couldn't recall seeing before, along with Fanta's Stevie Wonder cover and Yazoo's logo.

quote.text: Also very nice version of the ZoomScroller in here. You know how to do it!

summary: A 1K musicdisk for the Commodore 64 by Orb, coded and scored by 4mat: four tunes packed into a kilobyte, cycled with the space bar, with a minimal display of coloured bars and a scrolling label.
why: Sceners were struck by how listenable and well composed four tunes could be in 944 bytes, and several singled out the second tune. It's a good example of 4mat's size-limited music work.

quote.text: 4 tunes, 944 bytes? amazingly good quality of sound and composition.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Kitten Rescuers, SinDiKat and Invaders that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023, with code from Baze, Busy, mborik, Mike, Omega and Ped and music by Aki.
why: A first place at Forever 2023 from a large Slovak team effort, and its source has been made available.

summary: Arkos's two-disk-side Amstrad CPC demo from 2004, coded by Targhan (who also did the music and 3D graphics) with 2D graphics by Grim. It includes a pre-rendered 3D movie played back in blocky low-resolution colour.
why: A sizeable CPC production spread over two disk sides, mostly the work of one person. The on-screen text explains how the 2,400-frame movie was modelled on PC and squeezed in with a home-made delta RLE scheme.

summary: Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo that won the demo compo at ASCii 2004, with code and concept by Alff and music by Miguel.
why: A compo winner at ASCii 2004, and a demo built around a message rather than a showcase of routines, as its title and credited concept suggest.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo credited to Peppa Pig, with graphics by DMan, music by Nik-O and code and text by Kowalski. It won the 8Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2016 and stars the cartoon pig herself.
why: It took first place in the 8-bit demo competition at Multimatograf 2016. It's also a Spectrum demo built around multicolour mode, which gives finer colour detail than the stock attribute grid allows.
highlights: "i will break all that you can enhance"

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2015, with code from Noby, mborik, Busy, Mike and Omega and music by Aki.
why: A first place at Forever 2015 from a large Slovak-Czech team pooling several well-known Spectrum coders.

summary: Krap Gang's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2010, coded by Omega and Poke with graphics by Omega and z00m.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2010 that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode, with an Atari ST tune by Big Alec converted by Oedipus.
